title: e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with objective of strengthening use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Law and Justice

e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with objective of strengthening use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
31 JUL 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi

The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. Various ICT-enabled initiatives, including the Case Information System (CIS) 4.0, e-Filing, e Payments, Video Conferencing, Virtual Courts, Digital Case Records, National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS), eSewa Kendras, National Service and Tracking of Electronic Processes (NSTEP), the eCourts Services Portal and Mobile App, and other citizen-centric digital services, have been implemented across the High Courts and District Courts in a phased manner.

The e-Filing system is an end-to-end digital platform for the online filing of cases, written statements, replies and other related applications. As on 30.06.2026, the Rules for e-Filing have been implemented in 25 High Courts, including the High Court of Uttarakhand and the District Courts under its jurisdiction. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 1.25 crore cases have been filed through the e-Filing system across the country. The details of cases filed through the e-Filing system, High Court-wise and District-wise, is placed at Annexure-I.

(c):
 In the State of Uttarakhand, a total of 1.17 lakh cases have been filed through the e- Filing system before District Courts, including 356 cases efiled before the High Court of Uttarakhand. The District-wise details of cases filed through the e-Filing system in Uttarakhand, as received from the High Court of Uttarakhand, is placed at Annexure-II.

To create awareness and promote adoption of the e-Filing system across the country, the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in coordination with the High Courts, has undertaken training programmes, capacity-building workshops and orientation sessions for Judicial Officers, court staff, advocates and other stakeholders through the State Judicial Academies and the respective High Courts. User manuals, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), FAQs and video tutorials have also been prepared and disseminated to facilitate effective use of the e-Filing system.

Further, eSewa Kendras have been established across the country to assist litigants and advocates in registration on the e-Filing portal, scanning and uploading of petitions and supporting documents, online payment of court fees and availing other services relating to e-Filing, thereby promoting awareness and facilitating wider adoption of the e-Filing system.

This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.

***

Samrat/Pranab/Sagar
